seed: The recordings and sounds a video document has been given sit on the Library shelf, scope Media, as tiles with their name and length (video.html: b-roll.mov 0:04, music.wav 0:14). A tile stays on the shelf after its last clip is cut away, like a Premiere bin, and dragging it onto a track lands it at the moment and on the track under the pointer, with the same ghost, snapping and command-key insert as the file from the Finder. At Next defaults, no flag set.

steps.comment: View > Library, the way a person turns the shelf on: the Library waits to be asked for.

steps.note: An eight second screen recording on V1. The Library's Media shelf already holds it, as Tutorial Sample.mp4 with 0:08 in the corner of its picture

THE FIRST TEST: music brought in from the Finder and then deleted from the timeline. The Audio track is empty, and the music is still on the shelf as Sample Music.m4a, the way a Premiere bin keeps what the sequence no longer uses
THE SECOND TEST: the music tile held over the empty Audio track one second in. The lane shows the same dashed ghost a file from the Finder draws, the length of the music
THE THIRD TEST: the recording's own tile let go a few points short of the end of V1 snapped onto it, so the two clips butt together at eight seconds with an edit point between them
THE FOURTH TEST: with the command key held, the tile went in at three seconds and pushed everything after it along, exactly as a file from the Finder does
One Command Z takes the insert back whole
Picking the recording's tile opens its own section in the dock: its name, its length and how often the timeline uses it, its size, and Add at Playhead
THE FIFTH TEST: Add at Playhead put the recording at the playhead, two seconds in, on V1 (the track picked when the last clip landed), over what was there
